classification.difficultyReason: Model horizontal projection with the launch point as origin, eliminate time, then determine landing distance and impact direction.

content.prompt: An object is rolled horizontally from the top of a $20\text{ m}$ tower with initial velocity vector $5\mathbf{i}\text{ m/s}$. Use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the point of projection is the origin, find the Cartesian equation of the path.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find how far the object lands from the base of the tower.

answer.worked:
The ground is at $y=-20$.
$$\begin{aligned}-20&=-\frac{x^2}{5}\\x^2&=100\\x&=10\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$
The object lands $10\text{ m}$ from the base.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find, to the nearest degree, the direction of motion when it hits the ground.

answer.worked:
At the ground, $y=-20$.
$$\begin{aligned}-20&=-5t^2\\t^2&=4\\t&=2\text{ s}\end{aligned}$$
The velocity components are $\dot{x}=5\text{ m/s}$ and $\dot{y}=-20\text{ m/s}$.
$$\begin{aligned}\tan\theta&=\frac{20}{5}=4\\\theta&=\tan^{-1}(4)\approx76^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The direction is $76^\circ$ below the horizontal.
